scale_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the financial data section of our board deck by pulling current banking data from {{vendor}}, our startup banking/finance platform.

If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) which {{vendor}} account(s)/entity to pull data from if we have more than one, (2) the reporting period for the board meeting (e.g. current quarter plus trailing quarters for trend comparison), and (3) confirmation that your configured credentials for {{vendor}} are ready to use.

Using {{vendor}}'s API, please:
1. Retrieve current account/treasury balances across our business bank accounts.
2. Pull daily or periodic cash balance history covering the requested reporting period so we can show quarterly cash trends.
3. List transactions (or syncable transactions) for the reporting period, and where useful, retrieve details on specific large or notable transactions.
4. Organize the results into a clean summary: current cash position, cash trend over the period (e.g. burn rate or growth), and a breakdown of transaction activity by category or vendor if the data supports it.

Present the output as a structured summary (table or bullet list) suitable for dropping into a board deck slide, including: ending cash balance, period-over-period cash change, monthly burn rate if derivable, and top spend categories or vendors. Flag any data gaps, API errors, or accounts you couldn't access so I can follow up manually.

Done looks like: I have a concise, accurate financial data summary (balances, cash trend, transaction highlights) covering the requested period, ready to paste into the board deck, along with a note of any data you couldn't retrieve. Report back with the summary itself plus a short note on data completeness and any caveats about the numbers.

scale_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me pull revenue metrics for our upcoming board meeting deck. We use {{vendor}} as our payments/billing platform. Please use your configured credentials to connect to {{vendor}} and gather the following for the reporting period I specify (ask me for the exact date range and prior-period comparison window if I haven't given them):

1. Current MRR/ARR and trend over the last 6-12 months (use {{vendor}}'s analytics query capability — pre-built templates or direct SQL query against revenue data — to pull this).
2. Gross revenue, refunds, and chargebacks for the period, broken out separately.
3. Payout and balance-transaction data: pull each payout in the period and reconcile it to the underlying charges, fees, and refunds that make it up, so we can show net deposited amounts vs. gross bookings.
4. Net revenue after fees and reversals, itemized so finance can sanity-check the numbers.
5. Any notable anomalies (large refunds, failed payouts, unusual chargeback spikes) worth flagging to the board.

If you need my domain, account identifiers, or the specific reporting period, ask me before proceeding.

Output the results as a clean summary table (period, MRR/ARR, gross revenue, refunds, chargebacks, fees, net revenue, payout total) plus a short bullet list of anomalies or items needing finance's attention. Note any data gaps or periods where reconciliation didn't fully match so I can follow up with finance manually. Do not attempt to file, submit, or publish anything — this is purely a data-pull and reconciliation task to prep inputs for the board deck. Report back with the table, bullets, and a one-line confirmation of the date range covered.

scale_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a board meeting deck. I need a Profit & Loss (P&L) report pulled from our {{vendor}} accounting system for inclusion in the financials section.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear:
- Which {{vendor}} company/organization account to use (if we have more than one)
- The reporting period(s) required (e.g., the most recent fiscal quarter, year-to-date, or a specific custom date range the board wants to review)
- Whether comparison periods are needed (e.g., prior quarter, prior year, or budget-vs-actual)
- The output format preferred (PDF, spreadsheet/CSV, or both)

Then, using our configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} via its documented API and generate the P&L report for the specified period(s) and comparison(s). Pull the report in an open format (e.g., CSV or similar) so figures can be inspected or reused in the deck. If useful for cross-checking totals, also retrieve the underlying general ledger or trial balance data through the API.

Verify the report looks complete and internally consistent: revenue, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and net income/loss lines should all be present with no obvious gaps or zeroed-out categories that shouldn't be zero. Flag anything that looks off (e.g., missing categories, unusually large one-time entries) rather than silently including it.

When done, report back with: the period(s) covered, a summary of top-line figures (total revenue, total expenses, net income/loss), the file(s) or data exported and where they're saved, and any anomalies or discrepancies you noticed that I should review before this goes into the board deck.

Do not make any changes to the accounting records — this is a read-only reporting task.

scale_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare KPI and burn rate calculations for an upcoming board meeting deck. I'll provide (or please ask me for if missing): access to our accounting system (e.g., QuickBooks or Xero) and bank account data via configured credentials, our current cash balance, our latest monthly financial statements (P&L and balance sheet), and our current headcount/payroll figures. Also ask me for the specific KPIs our board tracks (e.g., MRR, ARR, churn rate, CAC, LTV, gross margin, active users, growth rate) if not already defined.

Using this information, please:
1. Calculate gross burn (total monthly cash outflow) and net burn (cash outflow minus revenue/cash inflow) for the most recent 1-3 months.
2. Calculate our runway (current cash balance divided by average net burn) in months.
3. Compile the core KPIs I specify, showing current period value, prior period value, and month-over-month or quarter-over-quarter change.
4. Organize all figures into a clean summary table suitable for pasting into a board deck, with clear labels and units.
5. Flag any figures that look anomalous (e.g., missing data, sudden spikes) for my review rather than guessing or estimating them.

Done looks like: a complete, accurate KPI and burn rate summary table with month-over-month comparisons, runway calculation, and clear notes on any data gaps or anomalies you found.

Report back with the summary table, the runway figure in months, a one-paragraph narrative summary of burn trend (improving/worsening and why), and a list of any data points you had to leave blank or flag for my confirmation before they go into the deck.

scale_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me draft our board meeting deck in Google Slides. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: (a) the link to our existing board deck template or last quarter's deck in Google Slides (or confirm you should create a new one), (b) our financial figures/reports for the period (revenue, burn, runway, cash balance), (c) key metrics/KPIs to highlight, (d) product update notes or a changelog, (e) current hiring plan/headcount changes, (f) the specific asks or decisions we want from the board this meeting, and (g) the target meeting date.

2. Using Google Slides (via the Slides app/API with my configured credentials), create or duplicate the deck and build out these sections in order: Cover/Agenda, Financial Summary, Key Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, Asks/Decisions Needed, Appendix (if relevant). Reuse our existing template's layout, fonts, and branding if a prior deck is provided.

3. Populate each section with the data I provide, formatting numbers into simple tables or charts where useful, and keep slide text concise (bullet points, not paragraphs). Flag clearly on any slide where data is missing or I still need to supply information (e.g., "[NEED: Q3 churn number]").

4. Do not invent numbers, projections, or claims — only use what I supply or what's already in the source deck.

5. When done, share the Google Slides link with me and provide a short summary of: which sections are fully complete, which have placeholders needing my input, and any inconsistencies you noticed versus the prior deck (e.g., metric definitions changed). This is a draft for my review — do not send or share it with board members.

scale_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 'Strategy and Asks' section of my board deck. I will author the actual strategic narrative and investor/board asks myself, but I need you to prepare everything around it so I can drop my content in quickly.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: my company domain, my current board deck file or template (Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Notion doc), and the current business priorities I want the section to cover (e.g. fundraising, hiring, partnerships, product direction) if I haven't already given them.
2. Build a clean slide/section template titled 'Strategy & Asks' with placeholder headers such as: Where We Are Today, Strategic Priorities (Next 2-3 Quarters), Key Risks/Decisions Needed, and Specific Asks of the Board (e.g. intros, hires, fundraising support, approvals).
3. Pull supporting metrics and context from the rest of the deck (financials, KPIs, hiring plan, product updates already compiled) and insert relevant callouts or data points into the template so I have evidence at hand when writing the narrative.
4. Draft placeholder prompts/questions under each header (e.g. 'What is the #1 strategic bet this quarter?', 'What specific ask do you have of each board member?') to help me structure my thinking, but do NOT invent or write the actual strategy text, asks, or decisions on my behalf.
5. Compile a short checklist confirming the section is ready for me to fill in: template built, supporting metrics linked, placeholder prompts inserted.

When finished, report back with: a link or file reference to the prepared section, a summary of what data/metrics were pulled in, and the checklist status. Then stop for human sign-off — I will write the actual strategy narrative and asks and review the final section before it's added to the board deck.

scale_005:n7.prompt:
You are helping me publish our compiled board meeting deck into our {{vendor}} board room workspace, using the documented public API or the {{vendor}} dashboard, with your configured credentials.

Before starting, ask me for anything missing: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/board room URL or parent page where the deck should live, (2) the finalized content sections to include — financials, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, and asks — either as pasted text/links or files I provide, (3) any specific formatting or template the board room already uses, and (4) which board members or roles should have viewing access.

Once you have these, draft the full board deck page in {{vendor}}: create a structured page with clearly labeled sections for Financials, Metrics, Product Updates, Hiring Plan, and Asks, using headers, tables, and embedded dashboards/widgets where useful to roll up metrics or portfolio progress. Organize it as a shared doc alongside our other project work, matching any existing board room structure or naming conventions.

Do NOT make the page live, publish it, change sharing/permissions, or notify board members. Prepare the page in draft form (or in a staging/private location if {{vendor}} supports it), and produce a checklist showing: the page structure, all section contents, any dashboard/widget links included, and the intended sharing settings.

This step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied — so after preparing everything, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the draft page link (or ID), a summary of what each section contains, any content you could not source and left as placeholders, and the exact permission/sharing changes that will take effect once approved.

scale_005:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT send) the email that delivers our board deck to board members, using {{vendor}} as our email platform, which I control via my configured credentials.

Before drafting, ask me for anything missing: (1) my domain, (2) the final board deck file or shareable link, (3) the list of board member email addresses (To/Cc/Bcc), (4) the meeting date/agenda highlights to mention, and (5) whether I want this sent immediately or scheduled for a specific time.

Once you have these, do the following:
1. Draft a concise, professional email in my voice that references the attached/linked board deck, briefly previews key topics (financials, metrics, product updates, hiring plan, asks), and states the meeting date/time.
2. Prepare the message in {{vendor}} (via its documented API or dashboard) with the correct To/Cc/Bcc recipients, subject line, body, and attachment/link — but do not submit it.
3. If I asked for scheduled delivery, set up the scheduled send within {{vendor}}'s scheduling feature, noting any undo-send grace window it offers, but leave it unsent until I confirm.
4. Compile a short checklist showing: recipients, subject, scheduled time (if any), and a summary of the draft body for my review.

Done looks like: a fully prepared, unsent (or scheduled-but-reversible) email in {{vendor}} plus a clear checklist I can review.

Because sending this email requires my explicit approval before it goes out, do not click send, submit, or finalize delivery yourself — stop for human sign-off once the draft and checklist are ready, and report back exactly what you prepared and what remains for me to approve.
